patch.value: Assert System.Rev on every write so a concurrent agent cannot silently overwrite another

Each update sends a JSON Patch document whose first operation is a test against the revision the local item was read at. Azure DevOps rejects the entire document when the revision has moved, which turns a lost update into a visible, retryable failure. The retry re-reads the work item, replays the intended field changes onto the new revision, and asserts again, so contention resolves without a human. This is the property that makes the package safe for many agents on one project.

A write whose asserted revision is stale fails and does not mutate the remote item; the failure is distinguishable from a transport error; a bounded retry re-reads and reapplies; a test interleaves two writers against a fake service and asserts the loser fails rather than wins

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Partially delivered by the scaffolding commit, and recording precisely which part, so this does not read as finished.

Done: every update patch leads with a test operation on the revision, an empty change set still asserts rather than becoming an unchecked write, the single write site refuses a document that does not assert, and a precondition failure is surfaced as a conflict exit code distinguishable from a transport failure. There is a test that interleaves two writers against a fake service on the same revision and asserts that the second one fails and mutates nothing.

Not done: the bounded retry that re-reads the work item, replays the intended field changes onto the new revision and asserts again. Until that exists, a caller sees the conflict and has to resolve it. That is safe but not yet the ergonomics this item asks for, so the item stays open.
